claims.text: Kanban manages work as a continuous flow through the stages of a board and does not need a fixed-length sprint or a sprint goal; an item is pulled into the next column when there is capacity for it.
claims.source_hint: glossary kanban; The Kanban Guide (2020): flow, pull; docs/team/kanban-board-example.md

claims.text: Scrum Guide 2020: the Scrum Guide contains the definition of Scrum; Sprints are fixed length with a Sprint Goal that no change may endanger; it prescribes no board or way to show the Sprint Backlog.
claims.source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020: The Sprint, Sprint Goal, Sprint Backlog

claims.text: docs/team/kanban-board-example.md@stage-1 lines 8-12 show four columns (Việc cần làm, Đang làm (giới hạn 2), Chờ review (giới hạn 2), Xong) with the listed items and developers; lines 24-28 explain that the support team (Dev 1, Dev 2) has no sprint and the feature team (Dev 3, Dev 4) keeps sprints. The (giới hạn 2) label means at most two items in the column (lines 14-19).
In Sprint 14, 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' did not finish and moved to the next sprint.

A sprint board shows the Sprint Backlog, which belongs to one sprint, so a new sprint brings a new set of items. Scrum and Kanban can be combined, e.g. Scrum roles and events with a Kanban-style board.
Sprint Planning starts the Sprint and is where the Scrum Team selects the work; the Scrum Guide describes the Daily Scrum, Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective as events.
